notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Polysomnography Report
Date: 03/14/2025
Patient: Ana María Coronado, 82 y/o F

Attended PSG 03/14/2025. Study reveals severe sleep-disordered breathing.
AHI 42.4/h. CA+MA 16% of total AHI. Oxygen desaturation nadir 82%. Total sleep time 345 min, sleep efficiency 78%.
Sleep stages: N1 12%, N2 50%, N3 15%, REM 23%. Periodic limb movements within normal limits.
No significant arrhythmias noted. CPAP titration recommended given severity.

Summary: Severe OSA with mixed apneas. Further management advised.

Sleep Medicine Consultation
Date: 08/10/2026
Patient: Ana María Coronado, 83 y/o F

Hx: Long-standing OSA dx, CPAP tx ongoing.

Current Tx: CPAP 10 cmH2O, residual AHI 27.2 despite nightly use = failure.

Assessment: Persistent moderate-severe OSA despite compliance with CPAP at 10 cmH2O.

Plan: Consider alternative therapies; evaluate for advanced PAP modalities or adjunctive treatments. Recommend sleep study reassessment and possible ENT referral for airway evaluation.

Follow-up: Schedule in 3 months or sooner if symptoms worsen.

Otolaryngology Consultation
Date: 09/26/2026
Patient: Ana María Coronado, 83yo F

82yo W referred for HGNS eval. PMH notable for mild HTN, no other significant ENT hx. Exam: Tonsils 1+, no other obstruction. Nasal passages patent bilaterally. Oral cavity unremarkable.

DISE 09/15/2026: AP velum collapse, no CCC. No significant tongue base or epiglottic collapse noted. Airway anatomy consistent with OSA findings.

Plan: Discuss HGNS candidacy with patient; consider further sleep study correlation and cardiopulmonary evaluation prior to device implantation. Follow-up scheduled in 4 weeks to review results and patient preferences.
